🇨🇦 AMD is buying Toronto's Taalas. Terms were not disclosed, and it still needs regulatory approval. Taalas was founded in 2023 by three former AMD employees who had been leaders at Tenstorrent. It raised $169 million USD in February and had taken about $219 million USD in total. The idea was to hardwire a trained model straight into silicon rather than run it on general-purpose GPUs. AMD says the technology goes into its accelerator roadmap. Look at AMD's year. MK1 in November, MEXT in June, FastFlowLM in July, Taalas now. Four inference deals in nine months, and Taalas is the second Canadian one after it took the Untether AI team in 2025. None of these had meaningful revenue yet. What is being bought is design talent, and it is concentrating into two or three balance sheets very quickly. The Toronto part is what I keep noticing. Untether's team went to AMD. Nvidia acquired CentML. Tenstorrent, founded here, is headquartered in Santa Clara. Ottawa's Hyperlume went to San Jose's Credo, and an SEC filing later showed the price was $92 million USD. AMD has had people here since it bought Markham's ATI in 2006. Four Canadian chip companies in two years. There was no Canadian buyer in any of them, and I would like to know whether one was ever asked.

July was my last month at Kodiak . The past 8 years have been exciting and incredibly rewarding. I started about 5 weeks after the company was founded with nothing but a laptop and a rack full of snacks, and led the company as CTO to the first full commercial launch of a driverless trucking fleet - 24/7 operations, owned and operated by the customer - in 2024, followed by Kodiak’s public listing on NASDAQ in 2025. As of June 2026, Kodiak had 35 driverless trucks deployed at the customer’s site, having operated 40,000+ cumulative paid hours without anyone in the cabin. The latest software release further increased efficiency by 30%, all in a harsh environment with oncoming, third-party traffic. And it also isn’t just the one vehicle, because not all customers want the same: we built several driverless platforms, from big semis to offroad vehicles, that could operate safely in their respective environments. Most recently, the team delivered the first driverless daycab that I know of, on yet another new OEM base platform and with a new Gen7 generation of autonomy hardware. This isn’t just technology, it’s a full product that is actually useful to customers - and that product focus has been in Kodiak’s DNA from day one. Behind the scenes, the reality of Physical AI is amazingly complex: It took designing a system from the ground up that could meet the rigor of a full safety assessment to launch in 2024 and repeatedly after; finding and hiring hundreds of excellent people to refine and execute the plan; coordinating OEMs, suppliers, contract manufacturers, and partners around the world and earning their trust over years; real-world testing in both hot and icy conditions from the Permian to Michigan, and many interstates between; testing in simulated environments that reflect all of those conditions with well understood fidelity; and aligning the software, hardware, and systems engineering so we could operate safely and efficiently at the same time. I was part of it at every step, leading, helping, and motivating; but the real credit goes to the team at Kodiak who did the hard work on the ground and made it happen. I keep being impressed by what this team is able to do, often on tight timelines and tighter budgets. I’ve seen first hand how listening well, sharing insights, and helping others grow will exponentially increase the impact of an organization. Thank you for giving me the opportunity and trust to lead you through the ups and downs every startup goes through on the way to success. It’s been an incredible experience! Now it’s time to make space for the next generation of leaders at Kodiak. I've been enjoying time with family, both here in the US and in Austria, and reconnecting with people I haven't had a chance to talk to for way too long. If you're around, let's chat - I'd love to catch up.

Major update from us at Extropic on our journey scaling #ThermodynamicComputing Our latest chip, Z1, is now taped out and in fabrication! Along with it, we are announcing edge-ready 0.5M pbit systems and 4M+ pbit PCIe cards. Z1 systems are coming in 2027. We plan to build a billion+ pbit cluster next year. On the software side, we are announcing Torx, a software framework for stochastic differentiable programming, essentially the stochastic computing equivalent of PyTorch. Check out docs.torx.ai Alongside Torx, we are announcing Thermalizers, our compiler for embedding Torx programs onto thermodynamic devices like Z1. The Thermalizers whitepaper is now on arXiv: https://lnkd.in/gkqDV-PB For all users: we just opened up an API where you can execute Torx and THRML programs on high-performance GPUs. You can try thermodynamic programming today at extropic.dev Thermodynamic computing is very real and scaling fast. Is your organization ready? Read more about the announcement here: https://lnkd.in/gDBq8V6b

Today I'm excited to introduce 224 Ventures , a deeply technical and GTM-focused venture firm investing in AI-native teams. We're launching with $100 million in assets under management. I'm building the firm alongside 224’s Frontier AI Partners Yann LeCun , Executive Chairman of Advanced Machine Intelligence, Professor at NYU, and Turing Award co-winner, and Oriol Vinyals , Discovery Loop co-founder and former Gemini co-lead at Google DeepMind. Investing exclusively through 224, all three of us will be actively involved with sourcing, evaluating, and voting on every investment. We've already begun backing technical founders across applications, robotics, infrastructure, and core intelligence—writing $1–5M checks as a collaborative investor, partnering alongside lead investors to back companies advancing the frontier of AI. Excellence spends time with excellence. The next generation of AI companies will be built by deeply technical teams. The strongest founders are most often discovered from within the communities where frontier AI research is happening. 224 is embedded in these communities, backing founders from the networks where the field itself is accelerating. This same philosophy shapes 224's LP community. Our LP base is made up of AI operators: frontier researchers, product and engineering leaders, chief AI/data officers, sales and marketing executives, and CEOs. These operators make up the hub of our ecosystem, one that reaches across nearly all of big tech, the Fortune 100, labs, and academia spanning the San Francisco Bay Area, New York, Paris, Toronto, London, and Tel Aviv. Together, our LPs form an operator network that helps 224 identify exceptional entrepreneurs long before they enter traditional venture pipelines. For our founders, this translates into a community of potential customers, design partners, co-founders, employees, mentors, and investors. Deeply grateful to our community who've chosen to build 224 with us. Shout out to Rebecca Torrence for the Bloomberg coverage. See link in comments.

I am joining Optica Industries as our director of hardware. Our objective: bring new technology to North American metals processing, and in doing so, be part of the solution to reemerging American manufacturing and hard-tech industries. I am joining because the founding team of Dylan Jin-Ngo , Sam Katz, and Henry Zhou sold me with their tenacity and vision. As a team of 3 the deals they've closed and strategic infrastructure they built in less than a year is undeniable. We are still an extremely lean team, but with a big vision, and some new funding that will be more broadly announced soon, we are shifting into next gear. If we can execute we will soon be responsible for supplying a significant portion of all recycled Aluminum in the country. For the past month I've been building in a garage in the Dogpatch. Consider joining me: we need support across EE, MechE, Optics, physics, and factory design. If you like heavy industry, robotics, factory automation, renewables/recycling, American manufacturing, hard-tech in general, (and processing railcars full of metal!!), reach out to me or Dylan.
